Set theory provides the standard formal foundation for mathematics (SEP Set Theory: "set theory has become the standard foundation for mathematics"; nLab: ZFC is "the orthodox foundations today"; Wikipedia ZFC: "the most common foundation of mathematics"). Foundational plurality preserved: category theory is a co-existing alternative foundation (edge:category-theory-formalizes-mathematics) — Noosphere records both and adjudicates neither as THE foundation (record-not-resolve).

Category theory is a co-equal alternative formal foundation for mathematics (SEP Category Theory: "a possible alternative to the standard set theoretical foundation for mathematics"; nLab structural foundations / ETCS). Most associated with Lawvere ETCS and topos theory and often described as a unifying framework rather than a strict ZFC-style foundation — the modest "alternative foundation" claim is what is asserted. Plurality with set theory (edge:set-theory-formalizes-mathematics) preserved, not adjudicated.

Mathematical logic supplies the formal languages, proof systems, and model/proof theory that formalize mathematical reasoning and proof (EoM: the branch concerned with "mathematical proofs and questions in the foundation of mathematics", enabling "the formalization of proofs on the basis of [a formal] language"; SEP Classical Logic: a logic = "a formal ... language together with a deductive system"). Scope note: mathematical logic is itself a branch of mathematics; this edge captures its formal-apparatus role for mathematical reasoning, not containment.

Probability theory provides the formal/mathematical foundation for (mathematical) statistics — estimation and hypothesis testing rest on it (Wikipedia: "Mathematical statistics is the application of probability theory ... to statistics"; EoM Mathematical statistics: methods of estimation/testing are "based on probability theory"). Distinct from the prerequisite_for edge (a learning order); descriptive statistics is less probability-dependent (scope caveat).

Probability theory (measure-theoretic, Kolmogorov 1933) gives the random-variable concept its formal definition as a measurable function on a probability space (EoM: "a random variable is nothing but a measurable function on a probability space"; nLab: "The formalization of this idea in modern probability theory (Kolmogorov 33) is to take a random variable to be a measurable function").

Probability theory formalizes the probability-distribution concept as a probability measure under Kolmogorov axioms (EoM: "Any such measure ... is called a probability distribution ... basic in the axiomatics introduced by A.N. Kolmogorov in 1933"; Wikipedia: "a probability measure on (X,A)"). The concept is partly internal to probability theory — a tight, near-definitional formalization (low information content, recorded).

First-order (mathematical) logic provides the formal framework in which axiomatic set theory (ZFC) is expressed (SEP Set Theory: "ZFC is an axiom system formulated in first-order logic"; Wikipedia ZFC: "Formally, ZFC is a one-sorted theory in first-order logic"). Generic relation (ZFC as a first-order theory); the converse grounding — set theory supplying model-theoretic semantics for logic — co-exists and is a separate relation.

Game theory provides the formal models of strategic interaction used throughout economics (Wikipedia Game theory: "the study of mathematical models of strategic interactions ... used extensively in economics"; SEP: game theory analyses how "interacting choices of economic agents produce outcomes"). Foundational text: von Neumann & Morgenstern 1944.

Game theory provides formal models of strategic political interaction / positive political theory (Wikipedia: "Early examples of game theory applied to political science are provided by Anthony Downs"; SEP: party-political polarization "is often modelled using game-theoretic logic"). Scope: formalizes the formal/positive-political-theory strand, not all of political science.

Evolutionary game theory (evolutionarily stable strategies, replicator dynamics) formalizes frequency-dependent selection (SEP Evolutionary Game Theory, Maynard Smith: "game theory is more readily applied to biology than to ... economic behaviour"; Wikipedia: EGT originated 1973 with Maynard Smith & Price).

Information theory provides the formal limits (channel capacity, coding) of communication/telecommunication (Wikipedia Information theory: "the mathematical study of the quantification, storage, and communication of ... information", formalized by Shannon's 1948 A Mathematical Theory of Communication; Wikipedia Channel capacity: "the theoretical maximum rate at which information can be reliably transmitted over a communication channel"). Two independent Wikipedia articles.

Information theory formalizes unconditional (perfect) secrecy (Wikipedia Information-theoretic security: "information-theoretically secure communication was introduced in 1949 by ... Claude Shannon ... who used it to prove the one-time pad system was secure"; Wikipedia Information theory lists cryptography among applications). Scope: information-theoretic (not computational) cryptography; computational crypto also rests on number theory (see edge:number-theory-formalizes-cryptography). Two independent Wikipedia articles.

Number theory provides the formal basis of public-key cryptography (Wikipedia Number theory: prime numbers "became the basis for the creation of public-key cryptography algorithms, such as the RSA cryptosystem"; Wikipedia RSA: "The security of RSA is related to the difficulty of factoring the product of two large prime numbers"). Scope: public-key/asymmetric cryptography. Two independent Wikipedia articles.

Probability theory is the formal substrate of the statistical-mechanics ensemble formalism (Wikipedia Statistical mechanics: macroscopic properties explained via microscopic parameters "characterized by probability distributions"; "The statistical ensemble is a probability distribution over all possible states"; nLab statistical mechanics: "an ensemble may be a probability distribution of similar physical systems"). Gibbs/Boltzmann.

Partial differential equations (Euler / Navier–Stokes) are the formal governing equations of fluid motion (Wikipedia Navier–Stokes equations: "are nonlinear partial differential equations"; nLab: "The partial differential equation describing viscous hydrodynamics").

Control theory formalizes the motion/feedback-control layer of robotics (Wikipedia Control theory: control theory "created new fields such as robotics" and its "Techniques ... are generally used to convert the higher-level tasks into individual commands that drive the actuators, ... using kinematic and dynamic models of the mechanical structure"; Wikipedia Robotics: "The control of a robot involves ... perception, processing, and action"). Scope: control layer, not perception/planning. Two independent Wikipedia articles.

Mathematical logic supplies the computability / formal-methods / type-theory core of theoretical computer science (Wikipedia Theoretical computer science: "closely related to mathematics and logic"; formal methods apply "logic calculi, formal languages, automata theory, and program semantics"; SEP The Church-Turing Thesis: "a fundamental claim in the theory of computability", computability is "formalism-transcendent"). Logic is one of several formal roots of TCS.

Mathematical logic formalizes programming-language semantics and type systems via the Curry–Howard correspondence (Wikipedia Curry–Howard correspondence: "a direct relationship between computer programs and mathematical proofs ... sets a form of logic programming on a rigorous foundation"; Wikipedia Semantics (computer science): formal semantics studies "the relation between computation and the underlying mathematical structures from fields such as logic, set theory, model theory, category theory"). Scope: semantics/type systems. Two independent Wikipedia articles.

Category theory formalizes typed/functional programming-language semantics (Wikipedia Category theory: "Many areas of computer science also rely on category theory, such as functional programming and semantics"; "a cartesian closed category is taken as a non-syntactic description of a lambda calculus"; Wikipedia Semantics (computer science): "Categorical (or 'functorial') semantics uses category theory as the core mathematical formalism"). Scope: typed/functional PL (monads, CCC), edge-of-envelope. Two independent Wikipedia articles.

Linear algebra (the Hilbert-space / linear-operator formalism) formalizes quantum information (Wikipedia Mathematical formulation of quantum mechanics: "This mathematical formalism uses mainly a part of functional analysis, especially Hilbert spaces, which are a kind of linear space"; nLab quantum information: "Hilbert space-based quantum information theory", "FHilb of finite dimensional Hilbert spaces"). For qubit/finite-dimensional QIS the apparatus is (complex) linear algebra; infinite-dimensional cases use functional analysis.

Statistics provides the formal inferential methods of econometrics (Wikipedia Econometrics: "an application of statistical methods to economic data in order to give empirical content to economic relationships"; Wikipedia Economics: economic theories "are frequently tested empirically, largely through the use of econometrics using economic data"). Near-definitional / low information content (econometrics is defined as applied statistics; cf. wave-1 C6). Two independent Wikipedia articles.

Dynamical systems (differential-equation models) formalize population dynamics in ecology (Wikipedia Lotka–Volterra equations: "a pair of first-order nonlinear differential equations, frequently used to describe the dynamics of biological systems in which two species interact"; Wikipedia Population dynamics: "a branch of mathematical biology, and uses mathematical techniques such as differential equations to model behaviour"). Adjacent relation `models`; the differential-equation framework formalizes the dynamics. Two independent Wikipedia articles.

Probability theory (stochastic processes) formalizes the asset-pricing / decision-under-uncertainty core of financial economics (Wikipedia Mathematical finance: derivatives pricing uses "risk-neutral probability ... continuous-time martingales ... Itō calculus, PDEs"; Wikipedia Financial economics: "centers on decision making under uncertainty in the context of the financial markets"). Scope: the probabilistic core; financial economics also has non-probabilistic (certainty/equilibrium) parts. Two independent Wikipedia articles.

Statistics / statistical learning theory provides a formal framework for machine learning (Wikipedia Machine learning: "Statistics and mathematical optimisation methods compose the foundations of machine learning"; "probably approximately correct learning provides a mathematical and statistical framework for describing machine learning"; Wikipedia Statistical learning theory: "deals with the statistical inference problem of finding a predictive function based on data"). Tension preserved (record-not-resolve): the weak claim (statistics provides A formal framework) is supported; the strong claim (ML = statistics) is contested — Breiman's "two cultures" (ML and statistics "closely related ... but distinct in their principal goal"). Two independent Wikipedia articles.

Mathematical optimization is the formal/mathematical core of operations research (Wikipedia Operations research: "Employing techniques from other mathematical sciences, such as modeling, statistics, and optimization, operations research arrives at optimal or near-optimal solutions to decision-making problems"; Wikipedia Mathematical optimization: "Another field that uses optimization techniques extensively is operations research"). Scope: optimization is one of several OR techniques but its formal backbone (LP/IP/convex). Two independent Wikipedia articles.

Probability theory (Bayes' theorem) formalizes Bayesian inference (Wikipedia Bayesian inference: "computes the posterior probability according to Bayes' theorem"; SEP Bayes' Theorem: "relates the 'direct' probability of a hypothesis conditional on a given body of data ... to the 'inverse' probability of the data conditional on the hypothesis"). Bayes' theorem is a theorem of probability theory.

Probability theory is the formal substrate of information theory — entropy is a functional of a probability distribution (Wikipedia Information theory: "Information theory is based on probability theory and statistics"; nLab entropy: "We can give a precise mathematical definition of the entropy in probability theory. Fix a probability space (X,μ)"). `formalizes` not `part_of`: information theory is a distinct field built on probability, not a subdomain of it.

Mathematics provides the formal framework for modern economic theory (Wikipedia Mathematical economics: "Economics has become increasingly dependent on mathematical methods"; "differential calculus and differential equations, convex sets, and graph theory, were deployed to advance economic theory"; parallel to the reviewed edge:mathematics-formalizes-physics). Tension preserved (record-not-resolve): the descriptive claim that economics IS mathematized is mainstream; the NORMATIVE "mathematization debate" is genuine — SEP Philosophy of Economics records Austrian skepticism "about the value of mathematical modeling"; the formalist-revolution critique (Blaug; Mirowski). No source refutes the descriptive claim, so supported with tension note, not disputed.

Husserlian phenomenology shaped existentialism — Heidegger, Sartre, and Merleau-Ponty adopted the phenomenological method (SEP Existentialism: "Following the core maxim of phenomenology introduced by his teacher Husserl, Heidegger's philosophy…"; IEP Existentialism: "Sartre… first encountered phenomenology, specifically the philosophical ideas of Edmund Husserl").

Greek philosophy (Aristotle, Plato) shaped medieval scholasticism (SEP Medieval Philosophy: the translations "of Aristotle… transformed the university syllabuses in the thirteenth century"; SEP Influence of Arabic and Islamic Philosophy on the Latin West: the Parisian arts faculty "declared all known works of Aristotle mandatory reading — a very influential move").

Pragmatism, through John Dewey, shaped philosophy of education (SEP Philosophy of Education: "John Dewey's conception of democratic education has had enduring influence"; SEP Pragmatism: "The giant figure in philosophy of education is of course Dewey, who pioneered it as a separate sphere of study"). Largely Dewey-mediated — a school-level influence carried by a central figure; a person/work node gate would let it be stated more precisely.

Analytic philosophy has critiqued/opposed continental philosophy, paradigmatically Carnap's critique of Heidegger (IEP Analytic Philosophy: it "found itself opposed both to classical Phenomenology… and also 'Continental'… philosophy"; SEP Heidegger: "Friedman (2000) argues that this disputation was the hypocenter of the subsequent analytical/continental divide"). Tension preserved (record-not-resolve): whether the analytic/continental divide is substantive or overstated/a caricature is itself debated — we record that the critique occurs, not a verdict on its fairness. The reverse direction (continental→analytic) is a separate edge, not yet independently sourced.

Experimental philosophy critiques the armchair/intuition method of traditional (analytic) philosophy (SEP Experimental Philosophy: x-phi "challenged aspects of non-empirical philosophical methodology, prominently including the use of intuitions as evidence"; SEP Intuition: the x-phi sources project is "often presented as a possible means of justifying skepticism regarding some class of philosophical intuitions"). Tension preserved: the critique's success is debated (restrictionist challenge vs intuition apologetics) and x-phi is internally divided over extending vs undermining the armchair method.

Feminist epistemology critiques mainstream/traditional epistemology — its conceptions of objectivity, knowledge, and reason as reflecting an androcentric perspective (SEP Feminist Epistemology: "Do mainstream philosophical conceptions of objectivity, knowledge, and reason reflect an androcentric perspective?"; IEP Feminist Epistemology: it "takes issue with the ways in which traditional epistemological paradigms derive from cases of simple and uncontroversial empirical beliefs"). Internal complexity recorded: postmodernist critiques of a unified feminist standpoint, and the critique-vs-extension question.

Cantor founded set theory in the 1870s (SEP Set Theory: "Set theory, as a separate mathematical discipline, begins in the work of Georg Cantor"; Wikipedia Georg Cantor: "Cantor's work between 1874 and 1884 is the origin of set theory"). Plurality preserved (record-not-resolve): SEP's early-set-theory entry quotes Zermelo crediting the theory as "created by Cantor and Dedekind" — Dedekind is a co-credited contributor and a candidate for a future founder node; this edge does not adjudicate sole authorship.

Kolmogorov gave probability theory its modern axiomatic foundation in 1933 (SEP Probability Interpretations: "Its axiomatization had to wait still longer, in Kolmogorov's classic Foundations of the Theory of Probability (1933)"; MacTutor Kolmogorov: his 1933 monograph "built up probability theory in a rigorous way from fundamental axioms in a way comparable with Euclid's treatment of geometry"). Earlier contributors (Borel, Lévy, von Mises) are recorded in the literature but the measure-theoretic axiomatization is Kolmogorov's.

Shannon founded information theory with his 1948 paper 'A Mathematical Theory of Communication' (MacTutor Shannon: "This paper founded the subject of information theory and he proposed a linear schematic model of a communications system"; SEP Information: optimal-coding theory "was already established long before Shannon developed its mathematical foundation (Shannon 1948; Shannon & Weaver 1949)"). Norbert Wiener's contemporaneous cybernetics overlaps but the field credits Shannon as founder.

Boole founded the algebraic tradition in logic, a co-founding strand of mathematical logic (SEP Boole: "George Boole (1815–1864) was an English mathematician and a founder of the algebraic tradition in logic"; MacTutor Boole: his 1854 'Laws of Thought' is "An investigation into the Laws of Thought, on Which are founded the Mathematical Theories of Logic and Probabilities").
